verdict.rationale: Lorikeet's own docs say the agent takes action through your APIs and MCP servers inside workflows. Its guardrails enforce workflow-scoped tool access and server-side identity validation in code, which covers the core of real API actions with scoped access. The scoping is per workflow rather than per-action auth, and specific refund, order-change and subscription-update actions are only implied, by a refund-workflow simulation example and a get-order-status tool test. Missing for 10: documented per-action auth or credential scoping, explicit docs for refund/order/subscription write actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, the agent takes real actions through my APIs — refunds, order changes, subscription updates — with scoped auth per action

citations.quote: The agent takes action through your APIs and MCP servers inside natural-language and deterministic workflows
Customer isolation, server-side identity validation, workflow-scoped tool access and hard execution caps are enforced in code rather than prompts
Connect Lorikeet in seconds to your ticketing system, knowledge base, and internal tools to seamlessly ingest data and take action for your customers
Build your customer Concierge to take actions inside the tools your team already uses
